article_title: The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology
citation: Norbaizura HARIS & Kamisah OSMAN. (2015). The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education, 16(3). https://tojde.net
title: Virtual Field Trip (VFT) module for Colonization and Succession in Mangrove Swamps
description: An interactive multimedia software programme designed by the researcher covering the Form Four Biology topic Colonization and Succession in Mangrove Swamps, targeting three syllabus objectives on colonization and succession processes, pioneer versus successor species, and mangrove plant adaptation. It integrates text, graphics, video and audio, a photo gallery, communication columns for contacting teachers, and links for deeper exploration, and can be "accessed by students repeatedly until students reach the desired objectiv es". In the study it was used in a computer lab with teachers acting as facilitators while students explored and then discussed the topic.
requirements: A computer lab with internet/software access so all students can explore the topics studied
Teachers available as facilitators to monitor students and answer questions during exploration
constraints: Designed for the specific Form Four topic Colonization and Succession in Mangrove Swamps, chosen because field study is the suggested curriculum activity for it
target_learning_goals: Describe the process of colonization and succession in mangrove swamps
Distinguish between pioneer and successor species in mangrove swamps
Identify adaptations of mangrove plants that survive in an extreme environment
examples: In the study, lessons began with an induction set, students explored the VFT module to seek answers to questions, teachers facilitated, and a discussion followed before the formative test
key_sources: Norbaizura HARIS & Kamisah OSMAN. (2015). The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education, 16(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1092841

article_title: The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology
citation: Norbaizura HARIS & Kamisah OSMAN. (2015). The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education, 16(3). https://tojde.net
title: Three-theory design framework for the VFT module: constructivism, information processing, and Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning
description: The article states that "The concepts of learning using a VFT include the theories of constructivism, information processing and cogniti on of multime dia learning." Constructivist elements include communication columns and exploratory links so students actively construct knowledge; information processing motivates repeatable access so information moves from sensory register through short-term to long-term memory via repetition and encoding, following Gagne (1985); and Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (dual channel, limited capacity, active processing assumptions) motivates combining text, graphics, video and audio to deliver complex and abstract concepts more easily.
requirements: Multimedia elements (text, graphics, video, audio) so learners process words and pictures in parallel channels
Repetition: the module must be re-accessible so students can extend limited short-term memory through repetition
constraints: The framework is the article's stated design rationale for this module; the article does not test the theories themselves
target_learning_goals: Understanding colonization and succession concepts in mangrove ecosystems through active, multimedia-supported construction of knowledge
examples: Reactive elements such as video are used to generate thought, build curiosity and enable deeper exploration of the mangrove swamp topic
key_sources: Norbaizura HARIS & Kamisah OSMAN. (2015). The Effectiveness of a Virtual Field Trip (VFT) Module in Learning Biology. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education, 16(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1092841

article_title: Comparing the impact of video feedback and group discussion on patient education performance among medical interns: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Managheb Seyed Esmaeil, Pouralimohamadi Neda, Taghipour Kaveh, Managheb Seyedeh Nastaran, Hosseini Hossein. (2025). Comparing the impact of video feedback and group discussion on patient education performance among medical interns: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07748-w
title: Video feedback workshop design: role-play, video recording, and independent self-assessment against a checklist
description: The VFB intervention consisted of six two-hour sessions with four participants per session, covering the same educational content and standardized scenarios as the comparison condition. Each scenario lasted "15 min for role-play and 15 min for video review and feedback": interactions were recorded, participants independently reviewed footage of their own interactions to identify strengths and areas for improvement, and self-assessed using a patient-education feedback checklist. The instructor clarified the checklist but did not assess participants or complete the checklist for them.
requirements: Patient-education feedback checklist provided in the workshops
Standardized scenarios and shared educational content
constraints: The instructor was not involved in directly assessing participants or completing the checklist
examples: Participants acted as physician, patient, and observers in role-play scenarios recorded on video

Comparing the impact of video feedback and group discussion on patient education performance among medical interns: a randomized controlled trial. article_title: Video-based feedback using real consultations for a formative assessment in communication skills.
citation: Dohms M. C., Collares C. F., Tibério I. C. (2020). Video-based feedback using real consultations for a formative assessment in communication skills. BMC Medical Education 20:57. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1955-6
title: Video-based feedback methodology combining problem-based interviewing and agenda-led outcome-based analysis in small peer groups with real consultations
description: The article describes a VF methodology grounded in Lesser's problem-based interviewing (PBI) model and agenda-led outcome-based analysis (ALOBA) feedback, in which "Each medical resident presented a pre-recorded interview in a real-life setting to a group of peers, subsequently receiving feedback from colleagues and two facilitators". Sessions ran about 90 minutes over roughly 10 weeks within a curricular formative assessment. Facilitators coordinated the session, helped residents verbalize their self-image, and supported microanalysis of micro-behaviors including exact words and non-verbal communication, while the group assisted in finding alternatives to less effective behaviors.
requirements: A facilitator who coordinates the session, helps residents perceive their self-image and perform self-assessment, and links feedback to communication theories
Pre-recorded consultations with real patients from a real-life primary care setting, taped close to the session date
constraints: The article was unable to causally link the intervention with its effects
The study lacked standardization of raters and SPs and had variation in local supervisors
target_learners: First-year medical residents in primary care residency programs
examples: Residents presented videos of real consultations with communication difficulties; the group paused the video when issues arose and the interviewer verbalized their self-image and analyzed communication micro-skills.
key_sources: Dohms M. C., Collares C. F., Tibério I. C. (2020). Video-based feedback using real consultations for a formative assessment in communication skills. BMC Medical Education 20:57. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1955-6
